newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forex deregulation may happen in 1998 - Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Forex deregulation may happen in 1998 - Sakakibara.

text.p: The deregulation of Japan's foreign exchange transactions will likely be implemented on April 1, 1998, when related tax systems are due to be revised, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Thursday.

Sakakibara said the deregulation of foreign exchange transactions will bring about intensified competition among banks. "I hope that Japanese financial institutions will be well prepared for more competition in the future."
He said forex decontrol will promote deregulation in other fields such as tax and securities transactions.

Tomomitsu Oba, subcommittee chairman of the Committee on Foreign Exchange and Other Transactions, an advisory panel to the finance minister, said he thinks deregulation will promote the use of yen internationally.
Sakakibara said the hollowing out of Japan's financial markets will accelerate unless the Japanese market liberalises. He said deregulation will certainly benefit Japanese people.
Oba said Tokyo's forex market is far behind that in London and New York.
Daily foreign exchange transactions averaged 167 billion dollars in Tokyo in April 1995, compared with 477 billion dollars in London and 266 billion dollars in New York, Oba said.
The number of foreign companies listed on the stock market in Tokyo amounts to 77 while London has 531 foreign companies and New York has 247.
Oba said the main purpose of the deregulation is to bring the Tokyo market to a level equivalent to London and New York.
Deregulation in foreign exchange transactions would encourage deregulation in other fields, Oba said.
